headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from Haystack’s MCP/network egress into Mem0’s memory workflows; no direct evidence of a shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs with broad network egress, so it can ingest external content that may later be treated as instructions. Mem0 is a knowledge-management component with no documented isolation or provenance controls here, so if Haystack-fed content is stored and re-read, prompt injection is plausible. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Haystack ingests untrusted web or tool output through MCP or REST and forwards it into Mem0 memory entries, injection content can persist.
IF Mem0 later reuses stored text as authoritative instructions without provenance filtering, malicious directives can influence downstream prompts.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every Haystack-fed memory item.
Strip instruction-like text before writing to Mem0.
Require human review for new memory sources.
Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted sources.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and provenance filters between Haystack and Mem0.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP endpoints, while Mem0 is a memory store that may retain whatever content it receives. Even though Mem0 shows no explicit egress, the pair can still move sensitive text from Haystack into persistent memory, creating a leakage path across work products. The exact shared workspace is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Haystack processes sensitive prompts, documents, or retrieved snippets and writes them into Mem0, those contents become persistent.
IF Mem0 is queried by other agents or users, stored sensitive text can be re-exposed beyond the original Haystack session.
mitigations: Limit Haystack inputs to non-sensitive data.
Configure Mem0 to exclude sensitive fields.
Review stored memories for secrets before enabling reuse.
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
requires-engineering: add redaction before persistence and access controls on memory retrieval.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and MCP/API access, but Mem0 shows no network egress and no write-capability surface in the profile. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely from the documented pair. Because Mem0 is not runnable here and no shared mutable resource is specified, the overlap is limited and the blast radius appears small.
conditions: IF both agents are later placed on the same writable workspace or database, concurrent updates could conflict.
IF an orchestrator grants Mem0 write access not shown in the profile, contention risk increases.
mitigations: Keep Haystack and Mem0 on separate resources.
Avoid shared writable directories.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator.
Document ownership of each mutable store.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency on shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can produce retrieved answers and route them through MCP/REST, while Mem0 is a memory system that may store and later surface those outputs. If Mem0 treats Haystack output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into future prompts and actions. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Haystack-generated text is written into Mem0 without validation, incorrect facts can persist.
IF downstream agents trust Mem0 memories as ground truth, one bad retrieval can propagate across sessions.
mitigations: Mark Haystack outputs as untrusted by default.
Require citation checks before memory writes.
Expire low-confidence memories quickly.
Review a sample of stored memories daily.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before Mem0 persistence and retrieval.

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics and has broad network egress, while Mem0 lists no data classes touched and no residency or retention mismatch is documented. There is no evidence of regulated data like PHI or EU PII in this pair, so compliance risk is limited to documentation gaps rather than a concrete violation. The other agent is not cited beyond the pair context because no specific mismatch is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is later routed through Haystack into Mem0, residency and retention requirements must be rechecked.
IF Mem0 stores data subject to deletion requests, its retention policy must be aligned before use.
mitigations: Confirm what data classes will be stored.
Publish a retention policy for memories.
Block regulated data until a DPA exists.
Audit logs for residency-sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows across both systems.
